tasks.short: Observe fish condition and pond or harvest status

steps.what: Observe fish and ponds for disease signs, growth, quality and harvest completeness

tasks.design: Retain direct observation of fish, ponds and harvesting conditions. Existing guidance in {DOCS} supports recognition and escalation; the digest's horticultural stock systems do not establish automated fish-health assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition and behaviour need interpretation in the actual pond or bed.
tasks.enabler_now: Order and labour tools do not replace biological observation.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle changes may have several causes and need specialist investigation.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor notices deviations and knows when to seek qualified animal-health support.
tasks.altitude: Observation responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Describe observed fish-health changes for specialist advice

evidence.claim: Retaining direct fish and pond observation is an E1 assessment from model knowledge; the digest supplies no applicable fish-health capability.

assumptions: Boundary is supervisor observation and judgement in an aquaculture operation, not laboratory diagnosis or workers' harvest labour.
No new sensor coverage, disease flag or structured fish-quality input is presumed.
Existing guidance remains; no custom monitoring system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow change is introduced.
unknowns: Species, production conditions and specialist support
research_questions: Which observed changes require immediate specialist investigation rather than routine follow-up?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Direct observation remains counted; no assumed camera or sensor runtime is treated as supervisor labour.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train forestry workers in equipment and safe work methods

steps.what: Train workers in felling, bucking, machine operation and safe loading practices

tasks.design: Keep practical forestry instruction, observation and correction with the qualified supervisor. Equipment and work-method references in {DOCS} support demonstrations; no generated course is treated as evidence of safe machine or felling competence.
tasks.previous_blocker: Safe technique must be demonstrated and observed under real site conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Information tools do not remove practical supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Terrain, loads and equipment condition can change the hazards.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor sees unsafe technique and intervenes immediately.
tasks.altitude: Practical training responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain recurring training needs from observed unsafe practices

evidence.claim: Keeping practical forestry training human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is forestry instruction delivery, not producing manuals or maintaining qualification records.
No structured safe-operator flag or automatic competence decision is assumed.
Existing approved methods remain; no custom learning tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. This task applies to forestry operations, not every sector named in the occupation.
unknowns: Equipment, site conditions and trainer qualification requirements
research_questions: Which worker errors require immediate intervention during observed practice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Demonstration, observation and correction retain all time; no guessed course-production share.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train aquaculture workers in rearing and harvesting methods

steps.what: Train workers in spawning, rearing, cultivating, harvesting and equipment use

tasks.design: Retain practical aquaculture demonstrations and supervised worker practice. Current methods in {DOCS} support training; no checklist completion substitutes for observing handling, cultivation and equipment use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Handling and rearing technique depend on species and production conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Document generation does not establish practical competence or animal-safe handling.
tasks.still_hard: Subtle handling errors can affect animal condition and harvest quality.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor spots unsuitable technique and adapts instruction to the actual stock and equipment.
tasks.altitude: Aquaculture training responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify a species-specific handling difficulty during training

evidence.claim: Keeping practical aquaculture instruction human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is direct aquaculture training, not staff records, manuals or the workers' production effort.
No free structured competence score or automated handling instruction is presumed.
Existing species and equipment guidance remain; no custom tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no process changes. Sector-specific training tasks are alternatives unless an operation actually performs multiple activities.
research_questions: Which handling skills require repeated observation before workers can perform them reliably?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Practical instruction stays counted; no existing equipment runtime or worker labour is counted as supervisor savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train agricultural workers in field methods and safety

steps.what: Train workers in planting, harvesting, weeding, insect identification and safety measures

tasks.design: Keep crop-specific field demonstrations, recognition checks and safety instruction with the supervisor. References in {DOCS} support the encounter; no image classifier or generated instructions replace observation of field work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Crop stages, field conditions and local pests affect practical technique.
tasks.enabler_now: Order and payroll tools in the digest do not establish a substitute for field instruction.
tasks.still_hard: Similar-looking insects and changing field hazards require contextual checks.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor corrects the worker's actual technique and recognises when identification needs expert help.
tasks.altitude: Field-training responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Describe uncertain insect observations for review

evidence.claim: Keeping practical crop-method and safety training human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is direct agricultural training, excluding manual authoring, payroll and worker production time.
No free insect label or structured worker competence flag is assumed.
Existing field guidance remains; no custom training system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. Apply this task to relevant crop operations and do not sum unrelated sector training by default.
unknowns: Crops, local pests and training requirements
research_questions: Which field techniques or insect distinctions workers cannot demonstrate reliably after instruction?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Demonstration, identification checks and safety instruction remain human; no hypothetical training-material savings.
